title: Decompose I/O billing steps and streaming pacing experiment
creator: Maya Chen
description: Run a structured experiment to evaluate decomposed per-direction pricing (input vs output) combined with a streaming pacing credit and minimum monthly reserve tiers for Hosted API customers. Goal is to find a pricing configuration that preserves revenue for heavy-output customers, reduces friction for high-ingress customers, and creates predictable enterprise contract language for minimums and security questionnaire disclosures.
hypothesis: If we bill input and output tokens at independently tunable rates and introduce a streaming pacing credit (small effective discount for streaming-first workloads) plus a tiered monthly reserve minimum for enterprise contracts, then we can: 1) reduce churn for high-ingress low-output customers, 2) increase realized ARPU from output-heavy workloads without driving significant usage migration, and 3) create contract-clauses that are clear for security questionnaires regarding measurement and auditability.
acceptance_criteria: A/B cohorts complete 8 weeks with statistically significant delta on churn or MRR at 95% confidence
Average cost per 1k generated tokens (P50) changes by <= 5% for baseline customers in cohort A
Enterprise pilot contracts (3 customers) accept minimum tier language without material redlines related to auditing token metrics
Streaming pacing credit does not increase 95th percentile latency violations or error rates on serving infra
metrics: Normalized revenue per 1M tokens (ingress vs egress split)
Percent of requests hitting streaming pacing credit threshold
Cost per token to Redwood (GPU cycles + amortized infra)
experiment_design: Two-arm A/B across hosted API paid customers with historical segmentation. Cohort A = control (current symmetric per-token pricing), Cohort B = experimental (input rate = 0.6x baseline, output rate = 1.4x baseline; streaming pacing credit = 15% effective discount for sessions that maintain <10 tokens/sec burst for first 5s; monthly reserve minimums applied to enterprise customers only: tiers 0/5k/20k monthly commit). Use 8-week duration, with simulation run on last 12 months of call logs to estimate power. Implement metering flags to track ingress/egress separately and streaming pacing eligibility. Run canary rollout behind feature flag; customers in pilot will receive explicit billing notice and a help article link.
rollout_plan: Week -4: finalize legal wording for reserve minimums and add security questionnaire Q/A draft
Week -3: implementation complete in billing service, metering telemetry in Console and eventstream
Week -2: internal smoke test with finance and infra (latency, billing correctness), PR #6742
Week 0: start 8-week A/B experiment for qualifying customers (randomized stratified by historical ingress/egress ratio)
Week 4: interim metrics review; if >10% infra regressions, pause and revert
Week 8: final analysis, customer interviews, legal contract pilots (3 enterprise customers), decision on rollout
risks: Customers misunderstand asymmetric rates leading to support volume spike
Edge cases in streaming pacing computation create billing disputes
Higher output rate causes increased infra spend; need to ensure cost pass-through does not erode margin
Enterprise legal requests additional auditability and may require changes to telemetry retention
